h: Ships, harbour and plenty more besides
p: Getting here couldn't be easier. Portsmouth Harbour railway station sits right by the entrance to the Historic Dockyard, so you can step off the train and be among historic ships within minutes. If you're driving, there's parking nearby, but the train saves a lot of hassle on busy days.

Inside the Dockyard, the museum sits alongside some world-famous neighbours. HMS Victory, Nelson's flagship at Trafalgar, is the star of the show for many. HMS Warrior, launched in 1860 as an ironclad warship, is another impressive vessel to explore, and the Mary Rose Museum tells the story of Henry VIII's warship and the remarkable objects recovered from the seabed.

For more naval history, take the short ferry across the harbour to Gosport, where the Submarine Museum and Explosion Museum of Naval Firepower round off the story. Over in Southsea, The D-Day Story explores the Normandy landings and Portsmouth's part in them, and the seafront is great for a breezy walk. With so much packed into one small corner of the city, it's worth planning a rough route before you arrive so you can pace yourselves.
